# Volume 4 — CHAPTER 21 BARRIERS SWEPT AWAY

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

“Nell,” Lorna uttered, suddenly interrupting a brief lull, “you have no idea how DELIGHTFUL it feels to sit beside you once more—busy at work—and chatting—and sharing quiet moments.”
{: #nw-v04-c21-p0000 }

In Nell’s garden beside the brook, they sat amidst the blue-eyed grasses. Past them, the sparkling water crooned, while dappled shadows were cast over them by the birches, and roses were in bloom along the walks. As the sun started to sink low, the air grew filled with a tapestry of music. A single melody came from the wind in the firs at the back of the house, a different one from the waves upon the bar, and yet another from the far-off bell of the church beside which the tiny, white lady slept. Even though it presently invoked sad thoughts, Nell was fond of that bell.
{: #nw-v04-c21-p0001 }

Her gaze turned attentively to Lorna, who had tossed aside her needlework and uttered her thoughts with a degree of freedom that was highly uncommon for her.
{: #nw-v04-c21-p0002 }

“During that dreadful evening while you were so sick,” Lorna continued, “it occurred to me repeatedly that maybe we would not share any additional conversations, strolls, or WORKS side by side. Then I understood precisely what your companionship had grown to signify to me—exactly what YOU signified—and what an unpleasant little monster I had been.”
{: #nw-v04-c21-p0003 }

“Lorna! Lorna! Calling my friends names is something I never permit anyone to do.”
{: #nw-v04-c21-p0004 }

“That is accurate. What you described is precisely what I am—a despicable small creature. Nell, I HAVE to share something with you. I imagine it will cause you to look down on me, yet I HAVE to admit it. Nell, during certain moments throughout this previous winter and spring, I actually HATED you.”
{: #nw-v04-c21-p0005 }

“I KNEW it,” Nell remarked serenely.
{: #nw-v04-c21-p0006 }

“Did you KNOW it?”
{: #nw-v04-c21-p0007 }

“Indeed, I observed it within your eyes.”
{: #nw-v04-c21-p0008 }

“And still you continued to like me and remain my friend.”
{: #nw-v04-c21-p0009 }

“Indeed, you merely despised me at times, Lorna. In the intervals, I believe your affection was mine.”
{: #nw-v04-c21-p0010 }

“I most assuredly did. Yet that additional dreadful sensation remained constantly present, ruining things, deep within me. I suppressed it—on occasion I did not remember it—yet on other occasions it would rise higher and overcome me. My hatred for you stemmed from my ENVY toward you—oh, at intervals I was utterly consumed with envy of you. You possessed a sweet tiny house—plus affection—plus joy—plus cheerful visions—all the things I desired—yet lacked entirely—and could not possibly attain. Oh, could not possibly attain! THAT served as the source of the pain. I would not have felt envy toward you, provided I possessed any EXPECTATION that my existence would at any point change. Yet I lacked that—I lacked that—and it appeared UNJUST. It caused me to feel defiant—and it inflicted pain on me—and for that reason I detested you at times. Oh, I felt such deep embarrassment about it—I am perishing from embarrassment at present—yet I failed to defeat it.
{: #nw-v04-c21-p0011 }

“During that evening, when I feared you might not survive—I believed I would face retribution for my evil—and my love for you was so strong at that moment. Nell, Nell, since my mother passed away, I had not possessed anything to love, save for the old dog belonging to Rufus—and having no object of affection is terribly awful—existence is incredibly EMPTY—and NOTHING exceeds the misery of emptiness—and my love for you could have been so great—and that awful event had ruined it—”
{: #nw-v04-c21-p0012 }

Lorna shook and became nearly unintelligible as her intense feelings overwhelmed her.
{: #nw-v04-c21-p0013 }

“Please, Lorna,” begged Nell, “oh, please refrain. I comprehend—let’s not speak about it further.”
{: #nw-v04-c21-p0014 }

“I must—I must. Upon learning that your life was saved, I swore to inform you the moment you recovered—that I would cease taking your friendship and company while hiding how little I deserved them. And I have felt such dread—that it might make you despise me.”
{: #nw-v04-c21-p0015 }

“There is no need for you to worry about that, Lorna.”
{: #nw-v04-c21-p0016 }

“Oh, I’m so glad—so glad, Nell.” To stop her brown, work-hardened hands from trembling, Lorna pressed them firmly together. “But now that I’ve started, I want to tell you everything. I don’t suppose you recall when I first laid eyes on you—it wasn't during that night on the beach—”
{: #nw-v04-c21-p0017 }

“No, that occurred the evening Hugh and I arrived back. You were guiding your geese down the slope. I certainly DO recall it! In my eyes, you were incredibly beautiful—for weeks afterward, I yearned to learn who you were.”
{: #nw-v04-c21-p0018 }

“I recognised who YOU were, even though I had never set eyes on either of you previously. News had reached me about the new doctor and his bride who were moving into Miss Russell’s small house. I—I despised you at that precise instant, Nell.”
{: #nw-v04-c21-p0019 }

“I sensed the bitterness in your gaze—subsequently I was uncertain—I believed I had to be wrong—since WHY ought that to be?”
{: #nw-v04-c21-p0020 }

“It was on account of you appearing so cheerful. Oh, now you will concur with me that I TRULY am a spiteful creature—hating a different female simply due to her joy,—and when her joy did not rob me of a thing! That reason accounts for why I did not ever pay you a visit. I was fully aware that I should visit—even the modest traditions of Seven Gulls required it. However, I was unable to. I was accustomed to observing you out of my window—I was able to glimpse you and your spouse walking slowly around your garden during the evening—or you rushing down the poplar lane so as to meet him. And I was pained by it. Even so, in a different manner, I desired to cross over. My feeling was that, were I not this unhappy, I could have been fond of you and discovered within you something I have not ever possessed during my existence—a close, GENUINE friend belonging to my own age group. And after that, do you recall that evening by the shore? You feared that I might deem you out of your mind. You surely believed that I was.”
{: #nw-v04-c21-p0021 }

“No, yet I was unable to comprehend you, Lorna. You pulled me close at one instance—and then you repelled me the next.”
{: #nw-v04-c21-p0022 }

“My spirits were very low that night. My day had been difficult. Rufus was exceedingly—exceedingly troublesome to handle on that occasion. Usually his disposition is rather pleasant and he is simple to manage, as you are aware, Nell. However, on certain days he is extremely different. My heart was so weary—the moment he fell asleep, I fled to the coast. That was my sole sanctuary. I remained there pondering the way my poor father had taken his own life, and asking myself if I might be forced to do the same eventually. Oh, black thoughts completely filled my heart! And just then you arrived, dancing beside the cove like a happy, carefree child. At that moment, I—I despised you to a greater degree than I ever have since. Even so, I longed for your comradeship. One emotion ruled me one instant; the opposite emotion ruled me the next. Upon returning home that evening, I wept from embarrassment over the opinion you must hold of me. Still, it has continuously been the exact same way whenever I visited this place. On occasion I would feel joyful and take pleasure in my call. Yet on different occasions that terrible emotion would ruin everything. There were moments when every single thing concerning you and your home caused me pain. You possessed such a quantity of lovely small items that were out of my reach. Would you believe—it is absurd—yet I felt a particular malice toward those porcelain dogs belonging to you. There were moments when I desired to grab Gog and Magog and smash their saucy black snouts against one another! Oh, you grin, Nell—yet it was not at all amusing to me. I used to come to this place and observe you and Hugh with your literature and your blossoms, and your domestic treasures, and your small private family humors—with your affection for one another evident in every glance and statement, even if you were unaware of it—and I would return home to—you are aware of what I returned home to! Oh, Nell, I do not think I am envious and resentful naturally. Throughout my girlhood I was without numerous items that my classmates possessed, yet I never minded—I never resented them because of it. Nevertheless, I appear to have become so malicious—”
{: #nw-v04-c21-p0023 }

“Lorna, my darling, do not accuse yourself any longer. You possess NO hatred or jealousy or envy. It is possible that the existence you are forced to lead has twisted you slightly—however, a spirit that was not as splendid and honorable as yours would have been destroyed by it. My reason for allowing you to confess all of this to me is my belief that speaking of it and cleansing your spirit will benefit you. However, cease accusing yourself now.”
{: #nw-v04-c21-p0024 }

“Indeed, I will not. It was simply my desire that you understand my true self. Nell, the most terrible moment of all occurred when you shared your dearest wish for the springtime with me. My conduct at that moment is something I will never pardon myself for. My remorse was accompanied by weeping. Furthermore, it is TRUE that I embedded numerous affectionate and fond thoughts of you within the small garment I crafted. However, I should have realized that whatever I created was destined to become merely a burial garment eventually.”
{: #nw-v04-c21-p0025 }

“Now, Lorna, that IS morbid and bitter—cast those ideas aside.
{: #nw-v04-c21-p0026 }

“It made me so happy when you carried over that tiny dress; and given that I was forced to part with little Joyce, I find comfort in knowing that she was clothed in the very garment you crafted for her at the moment you permitted yourself to care for me.”
{: #nw-v04-c21-p0027 }

“Nell, do you know, I think I will always care for you from now on. I do not believe I will ever experience that terrible feeling toward you any more. Discussing everything fully appears to have removed it, in a way. It is so odd—and I considered it so genuine and severe. It resembles unlocking a dark room's door to reveal a terrifying beast you thought was inside—and once the illumination pours in, your creature proves to be merely a shade, disappearing as the brightness arrives. It will never separate us again.”
{: #nw-v04-c21-p0028 }

“No, Lorna, we have become true friends now, and it makes me extremely happy.”
{: #nw-v04-c21-p0029 }

“I trust you will not misinterpret me should I add another thought. Nell, I suffered deep sorrow in my innermost heart when your baby was taken from you; and had it been possible to preserve her life for you by severing one of my hands, I would gladly have performed the act. Nevertheless, your grief has drawn us nearer to one another. The perfection of your happiness no longer stands as an obstacle. Oh, do not misinterpret me, my dearest—I am NOT joyful that your happiness has ceased to be complete—I can speak those words in all honesty; yet because it has changed, the chasm separating us is no longer so vast.”
{: #nw-v04-c21-p0030 }

“I REALLY comprehend that as well, Lorna. Now, we will simply seal away the past and erase whatever was disagreeable within it. Everything is about to change. Both of us belong to the race of Joseph now. I believe you have been remarkable—remarkable. And, Lorna, I am unable to refrain from trusting that life still holds something favorable and lovely in store for you.”
{: #nw-v04-c21-p0031 }

Lorna gave a shake of her head.
{: #nw-v04-c21-p0032 }

“No,” she uttered listlessly. “There is no hope at all. Rufus will not ever improve—and should he actually regain his memory—oh, Nell, things would turn out worse, still worse, than what we have at present. You are unable to comprehend this, you joyful bride. Nell, did Miss Winifred at any time inform you about the way I arrived at marrying Rufus?”
{: #nw-v04-c21-p0033 }

“Yes.”
{: #nw-v04-c21-p0034 }

“It makes me happy—I wished for you to be aware—yet I was unable to speak about it had you been unaware. Nell, it appears to me as though life has held bitterness ever since I reached twelve. Prior to then my childhood was full of happiness. Our poverty was great—nevertheless it bothered us not. Father possessed such splendor—he was extraordinarily intelligent, affectionate, and understanding. We had been close companions for as long as my memory extends. Furthermore, mother had such sweetness. Her beauty was truly immense. I resemble her, though my beauty falls short of hers.”
{: #nw-v04-c21-p0035 }

“According to Miss Winifred, you are much more beautiful.”
{: #nw-v04-c21-p0036 }

“She is wrong—or biased. I believe my own body IS superior—mother was frail and stooped from strenuous labor—yet her face resembled that of an angel. I would simply gaze up at her with devotion. Every one of us adored her,—father and Julian and I.”
{: #nw-v04-c21-p0037 }

It was recalled by Nell that a contrasting idea regarding Lorna’s mother had been conveyed to her by Miss Winifred. Yet, was the clearer sight not possessed by love? Even so, forcing her daughter into a marriage with Rufus Vane was indeed selfish on the part of Rose Ainslie.
{: #nw-v04-c21-p0038 }

“Julian was my brother,” Lorna continued. “Oh, I cannot express how much I loved him. And his life was taken in a cruel way. Do you know in what manner?”
{: #nw-v04-c21-p0039 }

“Yes.”
{: #nw-v04-c21-p0040 }

“Nell, his tiny face was visible to me when he was run over by the wheel. On his back, he fell. Nell—Nell—it is present to my mind right now. My eyes will never stop seeing it. Nell, my sole plea to heaven is for the erasure of that memory from my mind. O my God!”
{: #nw-v04-c21-p0041 }

“Lorna, do not mention it. I am aware of the tale—avoid delving into particulars that merely torment your mind to no purpose. It SHALL be erased.”
{: #nw-v04-c21-p0042 }

It took a moment of effort before Lorna recovered some degree of composure.
{: #nw-v04-c21-p0043 }

“Afterward, my father’s physical condition deteriorated and his spirits sank—he lost his mental equilibrium—have you also been told all of those details?”
{: #nw-v04-c21-p0044 }

“Yes.”
{: #nw-v04-c21-p0045 }

“Following that, mother was the sole reason I had left to go on living. However, my ambition was immense. My intention was to work as a teacher and pay my own tuition through college. My plan was to scale the utmost heights—oh, I shall refrain from discussing that as well. It serves no purpose. What transpired is known to you. I was unable to bear the sight of my precious, grief-stricken mother, who had spent her entire existence in toil, being evicted from her residence. Naturally, I possessed the ability to make a sufficient living for the two of us. Nevertheless, mother was INCAPABLE of departing from her home. It was there that she arrived as a bride—and her affection for father was so deep—and every one of her memories resided in that place. Still, Nell, whenever I reflect on the fact that I rendered her final year joyful, I feel no regret regarding my actions. Concerning Rufus—my sentiment toward him at the time of our marriage was not hatred—I merely harbored toward him the same unconcerned, pleasant regard I held for the majority of my fellow students. It was to my knowledge that he consumed alcohol to some degree—yet the tale regarding the young woman down at the fishing cove had never reached my ears. Had I known it, marrying him would have been IMPOSSIBLE for me, even for the sake of my mother. Subsequently—I TRULY came to despise him—however, mother remained unaware. Her life ended—and at that point I found myself completely solitary. My age was merely seventeen and I found myself completely solitary. Rufus had departed aboard the Four Sisters. My wish was that his presence at home would not occur very frequently in the future. A passion for the sea had continuously run in his veins. No other expectation remained for me. Indeed, Captain Saul carried him back home, as is known to you—and there remains nothing further to state. The truth about me is now clear to you, Nell—the most terrible aspects of me—every obstacle has been removed. And is it still your desire to be my friend?”
{: #nw-v04-c21-p0046 }

Nell gazed upward amidst the birch trees toward a half moon, resembling a white paper lantern, as it descended into the sunset's gulf. Her expression was exceedingly sweet.
{: #nw-v04-c21-p0047 }

“I am your friend and you are mine, forever,” she said. “A friend like I have never possessed until now. I have possessed numerous cherished and adored friends—yet there exists a certain quality in you, Lorna, which I failed to discover in any other person. You possess greater abundance to provide me from that wealthy essence of yours, and I possess greater abundance to yield to you than I possessed during my heedless youth. We are two women—and friends for eternity.”
{: #nw-v04-c21-p0048 }

Hand in hand, they shared a smile as tears welled up in both the blue eyes and the gray.
{: #nw-v04-c21-p0049 }
